title: A Long Story
english_paragraphs: I’m going to let you in on a little inside information. Everybody knows that footballers have text groups on WhatsApp. I have one just for my friends from home, and I have another just for my Barca teammates. But my favorite one might surprise you. Earlier this season, when we were already 8 or 9 points clear of Real Madrid in the league, I started a special group for some of the guys on the Spanish national team who play for Real Madrid and Barcelona.

If you only read what the media says, you would think that we hate one another. But, in fact, we all get along really well, and we text back and forth about tactics and football philosophies and even the books we’re reading.
…. No, come on, of course I’m joking! All we do in that group is talk shit to one another about Barça and Real!

It’s the best. We’re just like little kids. And the truth is, it’s especially hilarious for me right now, because now we’re up 15 points on Real in the league. So I’m getting very creative in my responses. Last season, when the Real guys were winning everything, they were feeling pretty good. They were talking shit constantly whenever I saw them at national team training.
Man, every time they won a match last season, they were posting shirtless photos on Instagram from the locker room. Remember that?

They were smiling and flexing their muscles like The Rock and saying #HalaMadrid and posting little trophy emojis. This season, though, it’s a different vibe. All their Instagram photos are looking very somber. “3 points today. We must keep working harder!”
So I’m texting them in the WhatsApp group, “Come on guys, why so serious?!”
Then I put a little crying emoji, and a laughing emoji.
I even made a special name for the group. It’s called: CONGRATULATIONS.

I can joke around with those guys, because they are my brothers on the Spanish national team. We might hate each other’s clubs, but we are all playing for the same country, with the same dream, and that’s something that I’m very, very proud of. Ever since I was a little boy watching Luis Enrique bleed all over his jersey at the’94 World Cup, my dream was to play for the national team.

I’m extremely proud to wear the badge every four years at the World Cup. Maybe that will surprise some people. If you watch television in Madrid, they’ll tell you a very different story about me. They’ll say that I’m a traitor, and that I want to tear the country apart because of my public support for the Catalan people’s right to vote in the independence referendum.

I have never even commented on how I would vote. I am not trying to be a politician and sway people. What I believe is irrelevant. I am just one opinion out of millions. But what I do believe is that the 7.5 million people from my homeland of Catalonia have the right to vote on this question in a peaceful manner. The issue is very complicated, and it requires a lot of thought and debate. It’s a tricky position for me to be in, personally, because the happiest moment of my life was winning the World Cup for Spain, but on the other hand, being Catalan is in my blood. That’s my people, my heritage, my land. And when 80% of people in Catalonia say they want the right to vote, I believe they should be heard. If that opinion makes my own countrymen dislike me… well, I am perfectly tranquil with that thought.
It’s funny, I noticed some people in America have started telling the NBA players to “just shut up and dribble” when they express their opinions on real problems in society.
It’s ridiculous, no?
It’s the same here in Spain. They say, “Just shut up and play football. It’s all you know.”

Sorry, but I will not just shut up and play. It’s not all I know. There’s a lot more depth to footballers than most people realize, and I think it’s important that we express ourselves and our views. Footballers are human beings, and that is something that is being lost in the media world that we live in today. There are things going on in our lives that the public has no idea about. Yes, you can google match results, and you can google transfer rumors, but you can’t google how a person feels, or what motivates them, or what they fear.
Let me give you some examples from my own life.
I look back on the last 10 years of my career, and I’ve won the World Cup, the Champions League, La Liga, the Spanish Cup… I’ve won it all, as I like to remind my Madrid friends on WhatsApp?
But 10 years ago, I was almost f***ed. My whole life could have turned out very different if it wasn’t for Sir Alex Ferguson.

I arrived at Manchester United a boy, and I left a man. It was a crazy time for me, because I had never been away from home before. I spent my first 17 years growing up in Spain in Barcelona’s youth academy, and it almost felt like I was playing for the local school team or something. I knew everybody there, and I was close to my family. So, to me, football was just fun. I didn’t understand the business side of the game at all. Then I arrived at United, and honestly, it was a complete shock.

One of my very first matches at Old Trafford, we were in the dressing room getting ready, and I was nervous as hell. Imagine it — I’m 18 years old, and I’m sitting in that little dressing room putting on my socks next to Ruud Van Nistelrooy and Ryan Giggs and Rio Ferdinand. I wanted to be invisible. I was thinking, Just do your job and go unnoticed.

So we’re sitting there waiting for the gaffer to come in and speak to us, and I’m literally sitting right next to Roy Keane. The dressing room is so small that our legs are almost touching. There’s no space at all.
It’s dead quiet. All of a sudden, you could hear this little vibration. Very soft.
Bzzzzzz……
………….. Bzzzzzzz.
Roy is looking around the room.
Bzzzzzzz…..
Oh, shit.
I realize it’s me. It’s my cell phone. I left it on vibrate, and it’s in the pocket of my pants, stuffed in the clothes bag that’s hanging right behind Roy’s head.

Roy can’t find where the noise is coming from. Now he’s looking around the room like a maniac. His eyes are darting everywhere, and he’s trying to figure it out. You know the famous scene with Jack Nicholson in The Shining, when he bursts through the door? That’s what he looked like.
He screams out to everybody, “Whose phone is that?!”
Silence.
He asks again.
Silence.
He asks a third time.
“Whose. Bloody. F*****g. Phone. Is. That?!”
Finally, I spoke up, like a little boy. Very softly, I said, “I’m so sorry. It’s mine.”
Roy put his arm around me, and he laughed, and he told me not to worry about it.
…. No, come on, of course I’m joking! Roy lost his mind! He went nuts in front of everybody! It was incredible. I almost shit myself. But it was a good lesson.

Now, in 2018, everything is different. All these kids are on their iPhones before the matches. But back then, in 2006? It was a different world. You didn’t do that. Especially not at United. Not in Roy’s dressing room. It was one of a thousand mistakes that I made when I was at United.

It wasn’t just the football that was difficult. It was the language and the culture and the loneliness. The isolation was the worst part. Being away from your family at 17, and being surrounded by grown men, by legends, by a manager like Sir Alex… it was very complicated. When people wonder why talented young footballers don’t make it abroad, I can assure you it usually doesn’t have anything to do with their technical quality. There’s always a lot more going on that you don’t see. The first two years I was in England, there were so many nights when I would come home from training and in Manchester it would already be dark outside at four in the afternoon, and I would be in my flat all alone. It was depressing. Then, of course, my mother would call me, and I’d lie and say, “Oh no, it’s going great, Mum. Everything is great.”
But it wasn’t going great. It was shit. I wanted to quit and come home to Spain. I remember during that time, my father always said something to me that was extremely important.
I’d complain to him, “I don’t know, Dad. The manager doesn’t trust me. These guys are so strong. I’m miserable.”
And he would say, “Well, you know what? Maybe today was bad. But the sun will always rise again tomorrow.”

I don’t know why, but it made me feel better. It kept me going. And I was very lucky, because, as naive as I was, and as raw as I was, Sir Alex was phenomenal to me from the very first day. The best managers all have this quality — even when they’re not playing you, and even when they’re hard on you — they make you believe that they really care about you. Sir Alex was like a second father to me. He made me earn it, but eventually he gave me my chance.

In 2007, after two years in England, he told me that I was going to play about 25 games that season. Everything started well. I was getting to play a bit alongside Rio. And then, in November, we went to play in Bolton.
Shit…
I can still picture the ball floating in the air.

It was a set piece. I was supposed to be marking Nicolas Anelka. Bolton chipped the ball into the box, and I thought, I’m going to be aggressive. I jumped up to head the ball away, and I completely missed it. It was like something out of a nightmare. The ball just… kept floating. It was that yellow and purple Premier League ball. Remember that one? It floated right over my head like a balloon.

I landed and turned around in horror. Anelka controlled the ball and scored easily. We ended up losing 1-0, and it was my fault. As a young defender, when you make a mistake like that, the manager simply cannot trust you anymore. Even if he wants to trust you, he can’t. I could tell, literally at the moment that Anelka controlled the ball, that I had lost the faith of Sir Alex, and probably the faith of most United fans.

Sir Alex promised me 25 games that season, and I ended up getting 12. It was an extremely difficult time. That mistake felt like the end of my career. It ended up being the beginning of it, but only because of what Sir Alex Ferguson did for me. You see, toward the end of that season, my agent told me that Barcelona were interested in bringing me back. Truthfully, I could not believe it. My exact words to him were, “That doesn’t make sense. I’m not playing at United, so why would they want me?”
And he said, “Well, they know you. They believe in you.”

Of course, I was thrilled. I wanted to go home. But I knew that I had to have a very difficult conversation with Sir Alex. There was no buyout clause in my contract, and United could set whatever price they wanted, so I had to convince him to let me go. It was one of the hardest conversations of my life, because he took such great care of me. But I walked into his office, and I was honest with him. I said, “Listen, I feel like I’ve lost your trust. Barcelona is my home. I want to go back. I hope you will let me go.”
We had a long conversation, and he decided that I was sincere, and he agreed to let me leave at the end of the season.

But that’s not the end of our story. Football can be very complicated. At the end of that season, guess who we had to face in the semi finals of the Champions League? Of course, it was Barcelona. I had no real chance of playing. I was the third-choice centre back. But right before the first leg at the Camp Nou, Nemanja Vidić came down with an injury. All of a sudden, I was going to have to step up and play in front of 90,000 people, against my boyhood club.
I was excited, nervous, shocked… everything.
Before the match, we had our usual two-hour siesta at the hotel. Of course, I couldn’t sleep. All of a sudden, there’s a knock at the door, and I look out the little hole…
It’s not the maid. It’s Sir Alex.

I knew something was going on, because he never came to see players before the match. I opened the door and he said, “Gerard, I regret to inform you that I can’t play you today. The deal is almost done. If I play you, and you have a bad game, they’ll say it’s because you’re headed to Barcelona. So I can’t put you in. I just want you to know why.”

The truth is, I was pretty devastated. Even though I wanted to go home, I was ready to give everything for United and Sir Alex in that match. It was my dream to play at the Camp Nou in the Champions League. It hurt very badly. But in the end, Sir Alex made the right decision. Everything worked out for the best for everyone. We got a 0-0 draw at the Camp Nou, and then we eliminated Barca at Old Trafford. We went on to win both the Champions League and the Premier League, and I was able to go home under very good circumstances.

Because of Sir Alex, I experienced one of the rarest things in football. I left in the best way possible. It didn’t feel like it at the time, but that mistake against Bolton was the best thing to happen in my life. In the end, Barcelona paid only $5 million for me. I arrived as the fourth-choice center back. No one expected much from me. But thanks to Pep Guardiola’s football brain and his belief in me, I was playing alongside Carles Puyol by the end of the season. Carles took me under his wing and was a huge influence on me. I learned so much from him, and we formed a partnership that extended to the Spanish national team.

If you would have told me when I returned to Barcelona that, in two years, I would be standing next to Puyol lifting the World Cup trophy, I would have thought you were absolutely crazy. But football is a funny business, and that is exactly what happened. That’s how quickly everything changed for me. And it really makes me think about fate. If I don’t make that mistake against Bolton, does it work out that way? If Sir Alex decides to keep me on for another season to get a bigger transfer fee for me, does it work out that way?

There are so many things that happen in a footballer’s life that people don’t see. And that’s why I’m writing this. And that is why I need to tell you another quick story… Because, as I said, football is very complicated. It’s not like the movies. When I was 24 years old, I was on top of the world. I had won everything — La Liga, Champions League, World Cup. I was playing under a genius manager in Pep Guardiola, who really believed in me from the moment I arrived. I was playing for the club I had loved since I was a boy. It was perfect.
And then…
I had the worst season of my career.

Everything seemed to fall apart in 2012. I don’t know why. Perhaps I had lost the fear that drove me to that level. But for whatever reason, I started questioning myself. As the season went on, Pep started to lose faith in me. For the first three seasons, we had a phenomenal relationship. I still revere Pep as a manager. But the truth is, it was an extremely hard time. He wanted his players to be obsessed with football 24 hours a day, and at that point in my life, I didn’t understand it. I wasn’t as committed to that philosophy. Pep simply didn’t trust me anymore, and the crucial moment was when he decided not to play me against Real Madrid in the league. That was crushing to me.
I started to think, Is this it? Is the dream of playing for Barca over? Is this how fast it can go away?

Then, in the second leg of the Champions League semifinal against Chelsea, something pretty crazy happened. Another turn of fate. We had lost 1–0 in the first leg at Stamford Bridge, and I didn’t play. Pep started me in the second leg at the Camp Nou to try to turn things around, but I honestly cannot tell you anything about the match.

Early on in the game, our keeper, Víctor Valdés, accidentally kneed me in the head during a clearance. I was knocked completely unconscious. When I got to my feet, I stayed in the game somehow, and I know that I ran around for about 10 minutes, but I truly cannot remember anything that happened. Eventually, the doctor noticed that I was struggling and they pulled me out and put me on a stretcher and rushed me to the hospital.
I woke up the next day, and I couldn’t remember anything from the match. I couldn’t even remember who won. I was in a complete fog.

It turns out, the match ended 2–2, and we were knocked out. Within a few days, Pep announced his departure from Barca. It felt like an era was coming to an end, and I thought that perhaps my time was up, too.

That season really made me think about my career, and my life. It was a wake-up call. When our team was playing for it all, Pep didn’t believe in me anymore. Then, when he finally turned to me, I got knocked out cold. Sometimes I think about what would have happened if I had woken up the next day and found out that we had gone through against Chelsea. I was out with a head injury for weeks, so I definitely wouldn’t have played in the final. Maybe we would have won the Champions League. Maybe Pep would have decided to stay at Barca. Maybe he never would have regained his trust in me. Maybe I would be at another club right now. Instead, Tito Vilanova arrived as the manager the next season, and he gave me a chance to regain my place.

There are so many moments like this that happen during a long career that make you think about fate, and chance, and how things could have gone differently. But that’s not what we read in the headlines. In the headlines, things are simple. In real life, the most interesting things are happening beneath the surface.
For example, people often ask me what it has been like playing with Messi for so many years. If I had to explain it in one sentence: He is an alien.
He is not from this planet.
He’s the only player that I can recall seeing play for the first time, way back when we were 13 years old, and saying to myself, “Oh, this kid comes from somewhere else. This is not human.”

He is an assassin. He’s the greatest I’ve ever seen. But, you see, it’s not about the way he attacks. People ask me, “What’s the most incredible thing I’ve seen Leo do on the pitch?” And they expect me to tell them about him dribbling three defenders. And trust me, I have plenty of those stories.

But for me, the reason that I know he’s from another planet is because of what happens when he doesn’t have the ball. Perhaps you can’t see it on TV, but I can see it on the pitch. You have to see his face when he’s sprinting to win the ball back from a defender. He has a look in his eyes that I haven’t ever seen in another footballer. It is what makes him so great. He is not interested in the spectacle. He rarely even does stepovers. He’s cut from a different cloth. His greatness is in his obsession with winning the ball.

Maybe that doesn’t make for a great headline. But when I think about Messi’s true magic, it’s not in something you can find on YouTube. It’s about a subtle expression in his eyes. His greatness would take me another 5,000 words to explain. Perhaps in another article!

And that brings me back to the beginning. As I get older and prepare for the final World Cup of my career, I have been thinking about my place in the world. I have been thinking about how I got here, and what else I want to accomplish in life.
As athletes, I believe that we should use our platform to connect with people and let them into our lives and into our minds a little bit more. I think this mentality is needed now more than ever.
If you watch television in Madrid, the media will tell you that everyone in Barcelona is trying to destroy the country.
If you watch television in Barcelona, they will tell you that everyone in Madrid is trying to oppress the people.
Everyone is the bad guy now, depending on where you watch TV.

They say the national team is in turmoil because of political differences. In truth, we almost never talk about politics. I’m too busy telling the Real guys that they’re f***ed in the league, and they’re too busy talking to me about refereeing conspiracies!

I’ve been a footballer for more than half my life. I’m 31 years old now. I used to say that I would be retired by 30. Honestly, do you know what keeps me going? It’s the experiences I’ve had in the locker rooms. It’s getting to know footballing geniuses like Messi, and Puyol, and Neymar, and Roy Keane (even though he almost murdered me).

In the end, football is a long trip. You win. You lose. You embarrass yourself. You make mistakes. You laugh, you cry. You do dumb things to pass the time. Maybe you and your teammates even set an assistant coach’s motorcycle on fire (before buying him a brand new one, of course… I’ll leave that story for another time!)
Hopefully, you grow from a boy to a man. This is what makes sports beautiful, for me. It’s all just one long story.
Welcome to The Players’ Tribune Global.
One of my goals is to never shut up.
chinese_paragraphs: 我要跟你们说一点内部消息。大家都知道，球员们 WhatsApp 上都有各种小群。我有一个只有老家朋友们的群，还有一个只有巴萨队友的群。但我最喜欢的一个群，可能会让你们吃惊。本赛季早些时候，当我们已经在联赛里领先皇马八九分的时候，我建了一个特别的群，把西班牙国家队里效力皇马和巴萨的几个家伙都拉了进去。
如果你只看媒体怎么写，你会以为我们互相恨透了对方。但事实上，我们处得非常好，会在群里聊战术、聊足球哲学，甚至连最近在读什么书都聊。
……不，得了吧，我当然是开玩笑的！那个群里我们干的事，就是互相损巴萨和皇马！
太好玩了。我们就像一群小孩子。而且说实话，现在这个节点对我来说尤其好笑，因为我们在联赛里已经领先皇马15分了。所以我回消息的创意，是越来越足了。上赛季皇马那帮人赢麻了的时候，他们感觉相当良好。国家队集训一见面，他们就逮着机会不停地损我。
兄弟，上赛季他们每赢一场球，就在 Instagram 上发更衣室里的裸上身合照。还记得吗？
他们笑着秀肌肉，跟巨石强森似的，配文 #HalaMadrid，再发几个小奖杯的表情。不过这个赛季，画风变了。他们的 Instagram 照片看上去非常沉重。“今天拿下3分。我们必须更加努力！”
于是我在 WhatsApp 群里问他们：“各位各位，干嘛这么严肃呀？！”
然后我再补一个小声哭泣的表情，和一个笑哭的表情。
我甚至给那个群起了个专用名。叫：CONGRATULATIONS（恭喜恭喜）。
我能跟那帮家伙开玩笑，因为他们在西班牙国家队是我的兄弟。我们或许恨死了对方的俱乐部，但我们为同一个国家而战，怀着同一个梦想，这一点让我非常、非常自豪。从小看着路易斯·恩里克在94年世界杯上球衣浸满鲜血的样子，我的梦想就是为国家队效力。
每四年能披上国家队战袍征战世界杯，我自豪至极。这可能会让一些人吃惊。如果你在马德里看电视，他们会讲一个关于我的完全不同的故事。他们会说我是叛徒，说我因为公开支持加泰罗尼亚人民投票独立的权利，就想撕裂这个国家。

可我连自己会投哪一票都从没公开评论过。我不是要当政治家，也不是要左右别人。我信什么并不重要。我只是几百万种意见中的一种。但我确实相信，我家乡加泰罗尼亚的750万人，有权利以和平的方式就这个问题投票。这个问题非常复杂，需要大量的思考与辩论。就我个人而言，这是个为难处境：因为我人生中最幸福的时刻，是为西班牙赢得世界杯；可另一方面，加泰罗尼亚人在我的血液里。那是我的同胞，我的传承，我的土地。当加泰罗尼亚80%的人说他们想要投票的权利，我认为他们应该被倾听。如果这个立场让我自己的同胞讨厌我……好吧，这个念头我也完全安然。
有意思的是，我注意到美国已经有人开始对NBA球员说“你只管闭嘴运你的球”，不让他们对社会上的真实问题发表看法。
很荒谬，不是吗？
西班牙这里也一个样。他们说：“你只管闭嘴踢球。你懂的只有足球。”
抱歉，我不会闭嘴，也不会只顾踢球。足球不是我懂的全部。球员的内心远比大多数人以为的丰富，我认为我们表达自己和自己的观点很重要。球员也是人——在今天的媒体世界里，这一点正在被遗忘。我们的生活里发生着许多公众完全不知道的事。是的，你可以谷歌比赛结果，可以谷歌转会传闻，但你谷歌不到一个人的感受、他的动力，或者他的恐惧。
让我拿自己人生里的一些例子来说吧。
回望我职业生涯的这十年，我拿过世界杯、欧冠、西甲、国王杯……该拿的我都拿遍了——这一点我很乐意在 WhatsApp 上提醒我的皇马朋友们？
但十年前，我差点就完蛋了。如果不是亚历克斯·弗格森爵士，我整个人生可能是完全另一个样子。
我以一个男孩的身份来到曼联，离开时已经是个男人。那段时间对我来说是疯狂的，因为我之前从来没有离开过家。我人生的前十七年在西班牙巴塞罗那的青训学院里长大，在那里踢球几乎就像在校队踢着玩。那里的人我全都认识，家人也近在身边。所以对我来说，足球就是纯粹的乐趣。这门生意的另一面，我完全不懂。然后我到了曼联，说实话，受到了彻底的冲击。
我在老特拉福德的头几场比赛之一，我们在更衣室里做准备，我紧张得要死。想象一下——我十八岁，坐在那间小更衣室里穿球袜，旁边是范尼斯特鲁伊、瑞恩·吉格斯和里奥·费迪南德。我恨不得自己隐身。我心想：做好你的事，别被人注意到。
我们坐在那儿等主教练进来训话，而我就坐在罗伊·基恩的正旁边。那间更衣室小到我们的腿几乎要碰到一起。一点空隙都没有。
鸦雀无声。突然，你听见一阵轻微的震动声。很轻很轻。
嗡嗡嗡……
罗伊环视整间屋子。
嗡嗡嗡嗡……
坏了。
我发现是我。是我的手机。我忘了关，调的震动，手机在裤子口袋里，裤子塞在衣物袋里，而那个袋子就挂在罗伊脑袋后面。
罗伊找不到声音是从哪来的。这下他像个疯子一样满屋子看。他的眼珠子四处乱转，拼命想搞明白。你知道《闪灵》里杰克·尼科尔森破门而入的那个著名镜头吗？他当时就是那副样子。
他对着所有人吼：“那是谁的手机？！”
一片寂静。
他又问了一遍。
寂静。
他问了第三遍。
“那。到底。是TM的。谁的。手机。？！”
最后，我像个小学生一样开了口。声音小得很，我说：“对不起。是我的。”
罗伊搂住我，笑了起来，叫我别放在心上。
……不，得了吧，我当然是开玩笑的！罗伊炸了！他当着所有人的面暴怒！场面太震撼了。我差点尿裤子。但那是很好的一课。
现在，2018年，一切都不同了。比赛前孩子们都捧着 iPhone。但在那时候，2006年？是完全不同的世界。你不能那么干。在曼联尤其不能。在罗伊的更衣室里更不能。那只是我在曼联犯下的一千个错误之一。

难的不只是足球。还有语言、文化，和孤独。孤立无援是最难熬的部分。十七岁就离开家人，身边全是成年人、传奇球星，还有弗格森爵士那样的主教练……那种滋味非常复杂。当人们疑惑为什么有天赋的年轻球员出国就踢不出来，我可以向你保证：通常跟他们的技术水平毫无关系。总有很多你看不见的东西在起作用。在英格兰的头两年，有太多这样的夜晚：训练完回到家，曼彻斯特下午四点天已经黑透了，我一个人待在公寓里。非常压抑。然后当然，我妈会打电话来，我撒谎说：“没事，一切都好，妈。好得很。”
但其实一点也不好。糟糕透了。我想过放弃，回西班牙老家。我记得那段时间，我父亲总对我说一句话，那句话对我极其重要。
我跟他抱怨：“我不知道，爸。主教练不信任我。这帮人身体太壮了。我很痛苦。”
而他会说：“哎，你知道吗？也许今天很糟。但太阳明天总会照常升起。”
不知为什么，这让我好受多了。它支撑着我走下去。我也非常幸运，因为尽管我那时又天真又毛糙，弗格森爵士从第一天起就对我好得不得了。最好的主教练都有这个特质——哪怕不让你上场，哪怕对你很严厉——他们都能让你相信，他们是真心在乎你的。对我来说，弗格森就像第二个父亲。他让我一步步去挣，但最终他给了我机会。
2007年，在英格兰待了两年之后，他告诉我，那个赛季我会踢大约25场球。一开始一切顺利。我开始能跟里奥搭档着打一些比赛。然后，11月，我们去博尔顿打客场。
糟了……
我到现在还能想起那个球飘在空中的样子。
那是个定位球。我本该盯防尼古拉·阿内尔卡。博尔顿把球吊进禁区，我心想，我要主动出击。我跳起来想头球解围，结果完全顶空了。就像噩梦里的场景。那个球就……一直飘着。就是那种黄紫相间的英超用球。还记得那个球吗？它像个气球一样，从我头顶飘了过去。
我落地，惊恐地回头。阿内尔卡停球，轻松破门。我们最后0比1输了，那是我的错。作为一个年轻后卫，当你犯下那种错误，主教练就再也无法信任你了。哪怕他想信任你，也做不到了。阿内尔卡停球的那一刻我就知道，我失去了弗格森爵士的信任，很可能也失去了大多数曼联球迷的信任。
弗格森爵士答应过那个赛季给我25场，最后我只踢了12场。那是极其难熬的一段时间。那次失误感觉就像职业生涯的终结。结果它成了职业生涯的开端——而这全靠弗格森爵士为我做的事。你看，那个赛季快结束时，我的经纪人告诉我，巴萨有意把我带回去了。说实话，我根本不敢相信。我对他说的原话是：“这不合理。我在曼联都踢不上球，他们要我干嘛？”
而他说：“哎，他们了解你。他们相信你。”
我当然欣喜若狂。我想回家。但我知道，我必须跟弗格森爵士谈一次非常艰难的话。我的合同里没有买断条款，曼联想开什么价就开什么价，所以我必须说服他放我走。那是我人生中最艰难的对话之一，因为他此前待我那么好。但我走进他的办公室，对他坦白了。我说：“听着，我感觉我已经失去了您的信任。巴萨是我的家。我想回去。我希望您放我走。”
我们谈了很久，他认定我是真诚的，同意赛季末放我离开。
但我们的故事还没完。足球可以是件非常复杂的事。那个赛季末，猜猜我们在欧冠半决赛碰上的是谁？当然是巴萨。我根本没有上场的机会。我是第三号中卫。可就在诺坎普首回合开打之前，内马尼亚·维迪奇伤了。突然之间，我得站出来，在九万人面前，对阵我少年时代的俱乐部。
我又兴奋，又紧张，又震惊……什么情绪都有。
赛前我们在酒店照例午休两个小时。我当然睡不着。突然有人敲门，我从门上的小孔往外看……
不是客房服务员。是弗格森爵士。
我知道出事了，因为他从不在赛前找球员。我打开门，他说：“杰拉德，我很遗憾地通知你，今天我不能派你上场。转会快谈成了。如果我让你上场，你又踢砸了，人们会说你是因为要去巴萨。所以我不能用你。我只是想让你知道原因。”
说实话，我相当崩溃。虽然我想回家，但那场比赛我本已准备好为曼联、为弗格森爵士拼上一切。在诺坎普踢欧冠是我的梦想。那一下真的很痛。但到头来，弗格森爵士做了正确的决定。结果对每个人都好。我们在诺坎普0比0逼平，然后在老特拉福德淘汰了巴萨。我们接着把欧冠和英超都收入囊中，而我也能在非常体面的处境下回家。
因为弗格森爵士，我经历了足球世界里最罕见的事情之一。我以最好的方式离开。当时不觉得，但对博尔顿的那次失误，是我人生中发生的最好的事。最后，巴萨只花了500万美元就把我签了回来。我回来时是第四号中卫。没人对我抱什么期望。但多亏瓜迪奥拉的足球头脑和他对我的信任，赛季末我已经在和卡莱斯·普约尔搭档了。卡莱斯把我护在翅膀底下，对我影响巨大。我从他身上学到太多，我们的搭档关系一直延续到西班牙国家队。
如果我回巴萨的时候你告诉我：两年后，我会站在普约尔身边举起世界杯——我一定觉得你彻底疯了。但足球就是这么有意思的行当，事情恰恰就这样发生了。我的境遇变化就是这么快。这真的让我思考命运。如果我没有在对博尔顿的比赛里犯那个错，事情还会这样发展吗？如果弗格森爵士为了多卖我一笔转会费而把我多留一个赛季，事情还会这样发展吗？
球员的人生里有太多人们看不见的事。这正是我写下这些的原因。这也是为什么我还需要再给你讲一个小故事……因为正如我说的，足球非常复杂。它不像电影。二十四岁那年，我站在世界之巅。我什么都赢过了——西甲、欧冠、世界杯。我在一个天才主教练瓜迪奥拉手下踢球，他从我到来的那一刻就真的信任我。我效力的是我从小爱着的俱乐部。一切完美。
然后……
我迎来了职业生涯最糟糕的一个赛季。

2012年，一切仿佛崩塌了。我不知道为什么。也许我丢失了那股把我推到那个高度的恐惧感。但不管什么原因，我开始怀疑自己。随着赛季推进，瓜迪奥拉开始对我失去信心。头三个赛季，我们的关系好得不得了。至今我仍敬重瓜帅这个教练。但说实话，那是一段极其艰难的时期。他要球员一天24小时都为足球痴迷，而在人生的那个阶段，我不理解这一点。我没有那么认同那套哲学。瓜帅就是不再信任我了，关键时刻是他决定在联赛里对皇马不让我上场。那对我打击巨大。
我开始想：就这样了吗？为巴萨踢球的梦就这么结束了？一切消逝得能这么快？
然后，欧冠半决赛对切尔西的第二回合，一件相当疯狂的事发生了。又一次命运的转弯。首回合我们在斯坦福桥0比1输了，我没有上场。第二回合在诺坎普，瓜帅让我首发，想力挽狂澜——但说实话，那场比赛的任何事我都讲不出来。
比赛early阶段，我们的门将维克托·巴尔德斯解围时一膝盖撞在我头上。我彻底失去了意识。我爬起来，不知怎么继续留在场上，我知道自己又跑了大概十分钟，但我真的完全不记得发生了什么。最后队医看出我不对劲，把我抬上担架，火速送去了医院。
第二天醒来，比赛的事我一点都想不起来。我连谁赢了都不记得。整个人一片迷雾。
后来才知道，那场球2比2，我们被淘汰了。几天之内，瓜帅宣布离开巴萨。感觉一个时代要落幕了，我寻思也许我的时代也到头了。

那个赛季真的让我重新审视我的职业生涯，和我的人生。它是一记警钟。当球队为一切而战的时候，瓜帅不再相信我。等他终于肯用我的时候，我被打得不省人事。有时我会想，如果第二天醒来，我得知我们淘汰了切尔西晋级了，会怎么样。我因为头部伤势缺席了几周，决赛我肯定打不了。也许我们会赢下那届欧冠。也许瓜帅会决定留在巴萨。也许他永远不会重新信任我。也许我现在人在另一家俱乐部。现实是，下一个赛季蒂托·比拉诺瓦来了，他给了我夺回位置的机会。
漫长的职业生涯里，有太多这样的时刻，让你思考命运、机缘，以及事情本可能怎样不同。但这不是头条里的世界。在头条里，事情都很简单。在真实生活里，最有意思的东西都藏在表面之下。
举个例子，人们总问我，和梅西一起踢了这么多年球是什么感受。如果要我用一句话解释：他是外星人。
他不是这个星球的人。
他是我唯一记得的、第一次看就让我对自己说“哦，这孩子是从别处来的”的球员——那时我们才十三岁。这不是人类。
他是个刺客。他是我见过最伟大的球员。但你看，关键不在他的进攻。人们问我：“你在场上见过莱奥做的最不可思议的事是什么？”他们期待我讲他连过三名后卫的故事。放心，那种故事我有一箩筐。
但对我来说，我知道他来自另一个星球的证据，是他无球时发生的事。在电视上你也许看不见，但在球场上我看得见。你必须看他的脸——当他冲刺着从后卫脚下把球抢回来的时候。他眼里的那种神情，我在任何别的球员身上都没见过。这正是他伟大的原因。他对表演没有兴趣。他甚至很少踩单车。他根本就不是同一种材料造出来的。他的伟大，藏在他对抢回皮球的痴迷里。
也许这上不了大标题。但当我想到梅西真正的魔力，它不是你在 YouTube 上能搜到的东西。它在他眼里一闪而过的细微神情。他的伟大够我再写五千字。也许下篇文章再写吧！
这又把话题带回了开头。年纪渐长，着手准备职业生涯最后一届世界杯，我一直在思考自己在这个世界上的位置。我一直在想我是怎么走到今天的，以及这辈子我还想完成什么。
作为运动员，我认为我们应该善用自己的平台，和人们连接，让他们更多走进我们的生活、我们的头脑。我觉得这种心态现在比以往任何时候都更需要。
如果你在马德里看电视，媒体会告诉你，巴塞罗那的所有人都在试图毁掉这个国家。
如果你在巴塞罗那看电视，他们会告诉你，马德里的所有人都在试图压迫人民。
现在，坏人在哪边都有，就看你电视开在哪个台。
他们说国家队因为政治分歧陷入动荡。实际上，我们几乎从不聊政治。我忙着告诉皇马那帮人这赛季你们完蛋了，他们也忙着跟我掰扯裁判阴谋论呢！
我当球员的时间，已经超过人生的一半。我今年31岁。我从前总说自己三十岁就退役。说实话，你知道是什么让我继续踢下去吗？是我在更衣室里经历的那些事。是能够认识梅西、普约尔、内马尔这样的足球天才，还有罗伊·基恩（尽管他差点杀了我）。
说到底，足球是一场漫长的旅行。你会赢。你会输。你会出丑。你会犯错。你笑，你哭。你干各种傻事打发时间。说不定你们全队还会把助理教练的摩托车点着了火（当然，事后又给他买了辆全新的……这个故事改天再讲！）
但愿你从一个男孩长成了一个男人。这就是体育之于我的美。这一切，本就是一个漫长的故事。
欢迎来到《球员论坛报》全球版。
我的目标之一，是永远不闭嘴。

sentence_pairs.en: I’m going to let you in on a little inside information.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我要跟你们说一点内部消息。

sentence_pairs.en: Everybody knows that footballers have text groups on WhatsApp.
sentence_pairs.cn: 大家都知道，球员们 WhatsApp 上都有各种小群。

sentence_pairs.en: I have one just for my friends from home, and I have another just for my Barca teammates.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我有一个只有老家朋友们的群，还有一个只有巴萨队友的群。

sentence_pairs.en: But my favorite one might surprise you.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但我最喜欢的一个群，可能会让你们吃惊。

sentence_pairs.en: Earlier this season, when we were already 8 or 9 points clear of Real Madrid in the league, I started a special group for some of the guys on the Spanish national team who play for Real Madrid and Barcelona.
sentence_pairs.cn: 本赛季早些时候，当我们已经在联赛里领先皇马八九分的时候，我建了一个特别的群，把西班牙国家队里效力皇马和巴萨的几个家伙都拉了进去。

sentence_pairs.en: If you only read what the media says, you would think that we hate one another.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果你只看媒体怎么写，你会以为我们互相恨透了对方。

sentence_pairs.en: But, in fact, we all get along really well, and we text back and forth about tactics and football philosophies and even the books we’re reading.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但事实上，我们处得非常好，会在群里聊战术、聊足球哲学，甚至连最近在读什么书都聊。

sentence_pairs.en: No, come on, of course I’m joking!
sentence_pairs.cn: 不，得了吧，我当然是开玩笑的！

sentence_pairs.en: All we do in that group is talk shit to one another about Barça and Real!
sentence_pairs.cn: 那个群里我们干的事，就是互相损巴萨和皇马！

sentence_pairs.en: It’s the best.
sentence_pairs.cn: 太好玩了。

sentence_pairs.en: We’re just like little kids.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我们就像一群小孩子。

sentence_pairs.en: And the truth is, it’s especially hilarious for me right now, because now we’re up 15 points on Real in the league.
sentence_pairs.cn: 而且说实话，现在这个节点对我来说尤其好笑，因为我们在联赛里已经领先皇马15分了。

sentence_pairs.en: So I’m getting very creative in my responses.
sentence_pairs.cn: 所以我回消息的创意，是越来越足了。

sentence_pairs.en: Last season, when the Real guys were winning everything, they were feeling pretty good.
sentence_pairs.cn: 上赛季皇马那帮人赢麻了的时候，他们感觉相当良好。

sentence_pairs.en: They were talking shit constantly whenever I saw them at national team training.
sentence_pairs.cn: 国家队集训一见面，他们就逮着机会不停地损我。

sentence_pairs.en: Man, every time they won a match last season, they were posting shirtless photos on Instagram from the locker room.
sentence_pairs.cn: 兄弟，上赛季他们每赢一场球，就在 Instagram 上发更衣室里的裸上身合照。

sentence_pairs.en: Remember that?
sentence_pairs.cn: 还记得吗？

sentence_pairs.en: They were smiling and flexing their muscles like The Rock and saying #HalaMadrid and posting little trophy emojis.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他们笑着秀肌肉，跟巨石强森似的，配文 #HalaMadrid，再发几个小奖杯的表情。

sentence_pairs.en: This season, though, it’s a different vibe.
sentence_pairs.cn: 不过这个赛季，画风变了。

sentence_pairs.en: All their Instagram photos are looking very somber.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他们的 Instagram 照片看上去非常沉重。

sentence_pairs.en: “3 points today.
sentence_pairs.cn: “今天拿下3分。

sentence_pairs.en: We must keep working harder!”
sentence_pairs.cn: 我们必须更加努力！”

sentence_pairs.en: So I’m texting them in the WhatsApp group, “Come on guys, why so serious?!”
sentence_pairs.cn: 于是我在 WhatsApp 群里问他们：“各位各位，干嘛这么严肃呀？！”

sentence_pairs.en: Then I put a little crying emoji, and a laughing emoji.
sentence_pairs.cn: 然后我再补一个小声哭泣的表情，和一个笑哭的表情。

sentence_pairs.en: I even made a special name for the group.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我甚至给那个群起了个专用名。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s called: CONGRATULATIONS.
sentence_pairs.cn: 叫：CONGRATULATIONS（恭喜恭喜）。

sentence_pairs.en: I can joke around with those guys, because they are my brothers on the Spanish national team.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我能跟那帮家伙开玩笑，因为他们在西班牙国家队是我的兄弟。

sentence_pairs.en: We might hate each other’s clubs, but we are all playing for the same country, with the same dream, and that’s something that I’m very, very proud of.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我们或许恨死了对方的俱乐部，但我们为同一个国家而战，怀着同一个梦想，这一点让我非常、非常自豪。

sentence_pairs.en: Ever since I was a little boy watching Luis Enrique bleed all over his jersey at the’94 World Cup, my dream was to play for the national team.
sentence_pairs.cn: 从小看着路易斯·恩里克在94年世界杯上球衣浸满鲜血的样子，我的梦想就是为国家队效力。

sentence_pairs.en: I’m extremely proud to wear the badge every four years at the World Cup.
sentence_pairs.cn: 每四年能披上国家队战袍征战世界杯，我自豪至极。

sentence_pairs.en: Maybe that will surprise some people.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这可能会让一些人吃惊。

sentence_pairs.en: If you watch television in Madrid, they’ll tell you a very different story about me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果你在马德里看电视，他们会讲一个关于我的完全不同的故事。

sentence_pairs.en: They’ll say that I’m a traitor, and that I want to tear the country apart because of my public support for the Catalan people’s right to vote in the independence referendum.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他们会说我是叛徒，说我因为公开支持加泰罗尼亚人民投票独立的权利，就想撕裂这个国家。

sentence_pairs.en: I have never even commented on how I would vote.
sentence_pairs.cn: 可我连自己会投哪一票都从没公开评论过。

sentence_pairs.en: I am not trying to be a politician and sway people.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我不是要当政治家，也不是要左右别人。

sentence_pairs.en: What I believe is irrelevant.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我信什么并不重要。

sentence_pairs.en: I am just one opinion out of millions.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我只是几百万种意见中的一种。

sentence_pairs.en: But what I do believe is that the 7.5 million people from my homeland of Catalonia have the right to vote on this question in a peaceful manner.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但我确实相信，我家乡加泰罗尼亚的750万人，有权利以和平的方式就这个问题投票。

sentence_pairs.en: The issue is very complicated, and it requires a lot of thought and debate.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这个问题非常复杂，需要大量的思考与辩论。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s a tricky position for me to be in, personally, because the happiest moment of my life was winning the World Cup for Spain, but on the other hand, being Catalan is in my blood.
sentence_pairs.cn: 就我个人而言，这是个为难处境：因为我人生中最幸福的时刻，是为西班牙赢得世界杯；可另一方面，加泰罗尼亚人在我的血液里。

sentence_pairs.en: That’s my people, my heritage, my land.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那是我的同胞，我的传承，我的土地。

sentence_pairs.en: And when 80% of people in Catalonia say they want the right to vote, I believe they should be heard.
sentence_pairs.cn: 当加泰罗尼亚80%的人说他们想要投票的权利，我认为他们应该被倾听。

sentence_pairs.en: If that opinion makes my own countrymen dislike me…
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果这个立场让我自己的同胞讨厌我……

sentence_pairs.en: well, I am perfectly tranquil with that thought.
sentence_pairs.cn: 好吧，这个念头我也完全安然。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s funny, I noticed some people in America have started telling the NBA players to “just shut up and dribble” when they express their opinions on real problems in society.
sentence_pairs.cn: 有意思的是，我注意到美国已经有人开始对NBA球员说“你只管闭嘴运你的球”，不让他们对社会上的真实问题发表看法。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s ridiculous, no?
sentence_pairs.cn: 很荒谬，不是吗？

sentence_pairs.en: It’s the same here in Spain.
sentence_pairs.cn: 西班牙这里也一个样。

sentence_pairs.en: They say, “Just shut up and play football.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他们说：“你只管闭嘴踢球。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s all you know.”
sentence_pairs.cn: 你懂的只有足球。”

sentence_pairs.en: Sorry, but I will not just shut up and play.
sentence_pairs.cn: 抱歉，我不会闭嘴，也不会只顾踢球。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s not all I know.
sentence_pairs.cn: 足球不是我懂的全部。

sentence_pairs.en: There’s a lot more depth to footballers than most people realize, and I think it’s important that we express ourselves and our views.
sentence_pairs.cn: 球员的内心远比大多数人以为的丰富，我认为我们表达自己和自己的观点很重要。

sentence_pairs.en: Footballers are human beings, and that is something that is being lost in the media world that we live in today.
sentence_pairs.cn: 球员也是人——在今天的媒体世界里，这一点正在被遗忘。

sentence_pairs.en: There are things going on in our lives that the public has no idea about.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我们的生活里发生着许多公众完全不知道的事。

sentence_pairs.en: Yes, you can google match results, and you can google transfer rumors, but you can’t google how a person feels, or what motivates them, or what they fear.
sentence_pairs.cn: 是的，你可以谷歌比赛结果，可以谷歌转会传闻，但你谷歌不到一个人的感受、他的动力，或者他的恐惧。

sentence_pairs.en: Let me give you some examples from my own life.
sentence_pairs.cn: 让我拿自己人生里的一些例子来说吧。

sentence_pairs.en: I look back on the last 10 years of my career, and I’ve won the World Cup, the Champions League, La Liga, the Spanish Cup…
sentence_pairs.cn: 回望我职业生涯的这十年，我拿过世界杯、欧冠、西甲、国王杯……

sentence_pairs.en: I’ve won it all, as I like to remind my Madrid friends on WhatsApp?
sentence_pairs.cn: 该拿的我都拿遍了——这一点我很乐意在 WhatsApp 上提醒我的皇马朋友们？

sentence_pairs.en: But 10 years ago, I was almost f***ed.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但十年前，我差点就完蛋了。

sentence_pairs.en: My whole life could have turned out very different if it wasn’t for Sir Alex Ferguson.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果不是亚历克斯·弗格森爵士，我整个人生可能是完全另一个样子。

sentence_pairs.en: I arrived at Manchester United a boy, and I left a man.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我以一个男孩的身份来到曼联，离开时已经是个男人。

sentence_pairs.en: It was a crazy time for me, because I had never been away from home before.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那段时间对我来说是疯狂的，因为我之前从来没有离开过家。

sentence_pairs.en: I spent my first 17 years growing up in Spain in Barcelona’s youth academy, and it almost felt like I was playing for the local school team or something.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我人生的前十七年在西班牙巴塞罗那的青训学院里长大，在那里踢球几乎就像在校队踢着玩。

sentence_pairs.en: I knew everybody there, and I was close to my family.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那里的人我全都认识，家人也近在身边。

sentence_pairs.en: So, to me, football was just fun.
sentence_pairs.cn: 所以对我来说，足球就是纯粹的乐趣。

sentence_pairs.en: I didn’t understand the business side of the game at all.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这门生意的另一面，我完全不懂。

sentence_pairs.en: Then I arrived at United, and honestly, it was a complete shock.
sentence_pairs.cn: 然后我到了曼联，说实话，受到了彻底的冲击。

sentence_pairs.en: One of my very first matches at Old Trafford, we were in the dressing room getting ready, and I was nervous as hell.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我在老特拉福德的头几场比赛之一，我们在更衣室里做准备，我紧张得要死。

sentence_pairs.en: Imagine it — I’m 18 years old, and I’m sitting in that little dressing room putting on my socks next to Ruud Van Nistelrooy and Ryan Giggs and Rio Ferdinand.
sentence_pairs.cn: 想象一下——我十八岁，坐在那间小更衣室里穿球袜，旁边是范尼斯特鲁伊、瑞恩·吉格斯和里奥·费迪南德。

sentence_pairs.en: I wanted to be invisible.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我恨不得自己隐身。

sentence_pairs.en: I was thinking, Just do your job and go unnoticed.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我心想：做好你的事，别被人注意到。

sentence_pairs.en: So we’re sitting there waiting for the gaffer to come in and speak to us, and I’m literally sitting right next to Roy Keane.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我们坐在那儿等主教练进来训话，而我就坐在罗伊·基恩的正旁边。

sentence_pairs.en: The dressing room is so small that our legs are almost touching.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那间更衣室小到我们的腿几乎要碰到一起。

sentence_pairs.en: There’s no space at all.
sentence_pairs.cn: 一点空隙都没有。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s dead quiet.
sentence_pairs.cn: 鸦雀无声。

sentence_pairs.en: All of a sudden, you could hear this little vibration.
sentence_pairs.cn: 突然，你听见一阵轻微的震动声。

sentence_pairs.en: Very soft.
sentence_pairs.cn: 很轻很轻。

sentence_pairs.en: Bzzzzzz……
sentence_pairs.cn: 嗡嗡嗡……

sentence_pairs.en: Bzzzzzzz.
sentence_pairs.cn: 嗡嗡嗡。

sentence_pairs.en: Roy is looking around the room.
sentence_pairs.cn: 罗伊环视整间屋子。

sentence_pairs.en: Bzzzzzzz…..
sentence_pairs.cn: 嗡嗡嗡嗡……

sentence_pairs.en: Oh, shit.
sentence_pairs.cn: 坏了。

sentence_pairs.en: I realize it’s me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我发现是我。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s my cell phone.
sentence_pairs.cn: 是我的手机。

sentence_pairs.en: I left it on vibrate, and it’s in the pocket of my pants, stuffed in the clothes bag that’s hanging right behind Roy’s head.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我忘了关，调的震动，手机在裤子口袋里，裤子塞在衣物袋里，而那个袋子就挂在罗伊脑袋后面。

sentence_pairs.en: Roy can’t find where the noise is coming from.
sentence_pairs.cn: 罗伊找不到声音是从哪来的。

sentence_pairs.en: Now he’s looking around the room like a maniac.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这下他像个疯子一样满屋子看。

sentence_pairs.en: His eyes are darting everywhere, and he’s trying to figure it out.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他的眼珠子四处乱转，拼命想搞明白。

sentence_pairs.en: You know the famous scene with Jack Nicholson in The Shining, when he bursts through the door?
sentence_pairs.cn: 你知道《闪灵》里杰克·尼科尔森破门而入的那个著名镜头吗？

sentence_pairs.en: That’s what he looked like.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他当时就是那副样子。

sentence_pairs.en: He screams out to everybody, “Whose phone is that?!”
sentence_pairs.cn: 他对着所有人吼：“那是谁的手机？！”

sentence_pairs.en: Silence.
sentence_pairs.cn: 一片寂静。

sentence_pairs.en: He asks again.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他又问了一遍。

sentence_pairs.en: Silence.
sentence_pairs.cn: 寂静。

sentence_pairs.en: He asks a third time.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他问了第三遍。

sentence_pairs.en: “Whose.
Bloody.
sentence_pairs.cn: 到底。
是TM的。

sentence_pairs.en: Phone.
sentence_pairs.cn: 谁的。

sentence_pairs.en: Is.
sentence_pairs.cn: 手机。

sentence_pairs.en: That?!”
Finally, I spoke up, like a little boy.
sentence_pairs.cn: 最后，我像个小学生一样开了口。

sentence_pairs.en: Very softly, I said, “I’m so sorry.
sentence_pairs.cn: 声音小得很，我说：“对不起。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s mine.”
sentence_pairs.cn: 是我的。”

sentence_pairs.en: Roy put his arm around me, and he laughed, and he told me not to worry about it.
sentence_pairs.cn: 罗伊搂住我，笑了起来，叫我别放在心上。

sentence_pairs.en: No, come on, of course I’m joking!
sentence_pairs.cn: 不，得了吧，我当然是开玩笑的！

sentence_pairs.en: Roy lost his mind!
sentence_pairs.cn: 罗伊炸了！

sentence_pairs.en: He went nuts in front of everybody!
sentence_pairs.cn: 他当着所有人的面暴怒！

sentence_pairs.en: It was incredible.
sentence_pairs.cn: 场面太震撼了。

sentence_pairs.en: I almost shit myself.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我差点尿裤子。

sentence_pairs.en: But it was a good lesson.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但那是很好的一课。

sentence_pairs.en: Now, in 2018, everything is different.
sentence_pairs.cn: 现在，2018年，一切都不同了。

sentence_pairs.en: All these kids are on their iPhones before the matches.
sentence_pairs.cn: 比赛前孩子们都捧着 iPhone。

sentence_pairs.en: But back then, in 2006?
sentence_pairs.cn: 但在那时候，2006年？

sentence_pairs.en: It was a different world.
sentence_pairs.cn: 是完全不同的世界。

sentence_pairs.en: You didn’t do that.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你不能那么干。

sentence_pairs.en: Especially not at United.
sentence_pairs.cn: 在曼联尤其不能。

sentence_pairs.en: Not in Roy’s dressing room.
sentence_pairs.cn: 在罗伊的更衣室里更不能。

sentence_pairs.en: It was one of a thousand mistakes that I made when I was at United.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那只是我在曼联犯下的一千个错误之一。

sentence_pairs.en: It wasn’t just the football that was difficult.
sentence_pairs.cn: 难的不只是足球。

sentence_pairs.en: It was the language and the culture and the loneliness.
sentence_pairs.cn: 还有语言、文化，和孤独。

sentence_pairs.en: The isolation was the worst part.
sentence_pairs.cn: 孤立无援是最难熬的部分。

sentence_pairs.en: Being away from your family at 17, and being surrounded by grown men, by legends, by a manager like Sir Alex…
sentence_pairs.cn: 十七岁就离开家人，身边全是成年人、传奇球星，还有弗格森爵士那样的主教练……

sentence_pairs.en: it was very complicated.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那种滋味非常复杂。

sentence_pairs.en: When people wonder why talented young footballers don’t make it abroad, I can assure you it usually doesn’t have anything to do with their technical quality.
sentence_pairs.cn: 当人们疑惑为什么有天赋的年轻球员出国就踢不出来，我可以向你保证：通常跟他们的技术水平毫无关系。

sentence_pairs.en: There’s always a lot more going on that you don’t see.
sentence_pairs.cn: 总有很多你看不见的东西在起作用。

sentence_pairs.en: The first two years I was in England, there were so many nights when I would come home from training and in Manchester it would already be dark outside at four in the afternoon, and I would be in my flat all alone.
sentence_pairs.cn: 在英格兰的头两年，有太多这样的夜晚：训练完回到家，曼彻斯特下午四点天已经黑透了，我一个人待在公寓里。

sentence_pairs.en: It was depressing.
sentence_pairs.cn: 非常压抑。

sentence_pairs.en: Then, of course, my mother would call me, and I’d lie and say, “Oh no, it’s going great, Mum.
sentence_pairs.cn: 然后当然，我妈会打电话来，我撒谎说：“没事，一切都好，妈。

sentence_pairs.en: Everything is great.”
sentence_pairs.cn: 好得很。”

sentence_pairs.en: But it wasn’t going great.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但其实一点也不好。

sentence_pairs.en: It was shit.
sentence_pairs.cn: 糟糕透了。

sentence_pairs.en: I wanted to quit and come home to Spain.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我想过放弃，回西班牙老家。

sentence_pairs.en: I remember during that time, my father always said something to me that was extremely important.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我记得那段时间，我父亲总对我说一句话，那句话对我极其重要。

sentence_pairs.en: I’d complain to him, “I don’t know, Dad.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我跟他抱怨：“我不知道，爸。

sentence_pairs.en: The manager doesn’t trust me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 主教练不信任我。

sentence_pairs.en: These guys are so strong.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这帮人身体太壮了。

sentence_pairs.en: I’m miserable.”
sentence_pairs.cn: 我很痛苦。”

sentence_pairs.en: And he would say, “Well, you know what?
sentence_pairs.cn: 而他会说：“哎，你知道吗？

sentence_pairs.en: Maybe today was bad.
sentence_pairs.cn: 也许今天很糟。

sentence_pairs.en: But the sun will always rise again tomorrow.”
sentence_pairs.cn: 但太阳明天总会照常升起。”

sentence_pairs.en: I don’t know why, but it made me feel better.
sentence_pairs.cn: 不知为什么，这让我好受多了。

sentence_pairs.en: It kept me going.
sentence_pairs.cn: 它支撑着我走下去。

sentence_pairs.en: And I was very lucky, because, as naive as I was, and as raw as I was, Sir Alex was phenomenal to me from the very first day.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我也非常幸运，因为尽管我那时又天真又毛糙，弗格森爵士从第一天起就对我好得不得了。

sentence_pairs.en: The best managers all have this quality — even when they’re not playing you, and even when they’re hard on you — they make you believe that they really care about you.
sentence_pairs.cn: 最好的主教练都有这个特质——哪怕不让你上场，哪怕对你很严厉——他们都能让你相信，他们是真心在乎你的。

sentence_pairs.en: Sir Alex was like a second father to me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 对我来说，弗格森就像第二个父亲。

sentence_pairs.en: He made me earn it, but eventually he gave me my chance.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他让我一步步去挣，但最终他给了我机会。

sentence_pairs.en: In 2007, after two years in England, he told me that I was going to play about 25 games that season.
sentence_pairs.cn: 2007年，在英格兰待了两年之后，他告诉我，那个赛季我会踢大约25场球。

sentence_pairs.en: Everything started well.
sentence_pairs.cn: 一开始一切顺利。

sentence_pairs.en: I was getting to play a bit alongside Rio.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我开始能跟里奥搭档着打一些比赛。

sentence_pairs.en: And then, in November, we went to play in Bolton.
sentence_pairs.cn: 然后，11月，我们去博尔顿打客场。

sentence_pairs.en: Shit…
sentence_pairs.cn: 糟了……

sentence_pairs.en: I can still picture the ball floating in the air.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我到现在还能想起那个球飘在空中的样子。

sentence_pairs.en: It was a set piece.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那是个定位球。

sentence_pairs.en: I was supposed to be marking Nicolas Anelka.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我本该盯防尼古拉·阿内尔卡。

sentence_pairs.en: Bolton chipped the ball into the box, and I thought, I’m going to be aggressive.
sentence_pairs.cn: 博尔顿把球吊进禁区，我心想，我要主动出击。

sentence_pairs.en: I jumped up to head the ball away, and I completely missed it.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我跳起来想头球解围，结果完全顶空了。

sentence_pairs.en: It was like something out of a nightmare.
sentence_pairs.cn: 就像噩梦里的场景。

sentence_pairs.en: The ball just…
sentence_pairs.cn: 那个球就……

sentence_pairs.en: kept floating.
sentence_pairs.cn: 一直飘着。

sentence_pairs.en: It was that yellow and purple Premier League ball.
sentence_pairs.cn: 就是那种黄紫相间的英超用球。

sentence_pairs.en: Remember that one?
sentence_pairs.cn: 还记得那个球吗？

sentence_pairs.en: It floated right over my head like a balloon.
sentence_pairs.cn: 它像个气球一样，从我头顶飘了过去。

sentence_pairs.en: I landed and turned around in horror.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我落地，惊恐地回头。

sentence_pairs.en: Anelka controlled the ball and scored easily.
sentence_pairs.cn: 阿内尔卡停球，轻松破门。

sentence_pairs.en: We ended up losing 1-0, and it was my fault.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我们最后0比1输了，那是我的错。

sentence_pairs.en: As a young defender, when you make a mistake like that, the manager simply cannot trust you anymore.
sentence_pairs.cn: 作为一个年轻后卫，当你犯下那种错误，主教练就再也无法信任你了。

sentence_pairs.en: Even if he wants to trust you, he can’t.
sentence_pairs.cn: 哪怕他想信任你，也做不到了。

sentence_pairs.en: I could tell, literally at the moment that Anelka controlled the ball, that I had lost the faith of Sir Alex, and probably the faith of most United fans.
sentence_pairs.cn: 阿内尔卡停球的那一刻我就知道，我失去了弗格森爵士的信任，很可能也失去了大多数曼联球迷的信任。

sentence_pairs.en: Sir Alex promised me 25 games that season, and I ended up getting 12.
sentence_pairs.cn: 弗格森爵士答应过那个赛季给我25场，最后我只踢了12场。

sentence_pairs.en: It was an extremely difficult time.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那是极其难熬的一段时间。

sentence_pairs.en: That mistake felt like the end of my career.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那次失误感觉就像职业生涯的终结。

sentence_pairs.en: It ended up being the beginning of it, but only because of what Sir Alex Ferguson did for me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 结果它成了职业生涯的开端——而这全靠弗格森爵士为我做的事。

sentence_pairs.en: You see, toward the end of that season, my agent told me that Barcelona were interested in bringing me back.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你看，那个赛季快结束时，我的经纪人告诉我，巴萨有意把我带回去了。

sentence_pairs.en: Truthfully, I could not believe it.
sentence_pairs.cn: 说实话，我根本不敢相信。

sentence_pairs.en: My exact words to him were, “That doesn’t make sense.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我对他说的原话是：“这不合理。

sentence_pairs.en: I’m not playing at United, so why would they want me?”
sentence_pairs.cn: 我在曼联都踢不上球，他们要我干嘛？”

sentence_pairs.en: And he said, “Well, they know you.
sentence_pairs.cn: 而他说：“哎，他们了解你。

sentence_pairs.en: They believe in you.”
sentence_pairs.cn: 他们相信你。”

sentence_pairs.en: Of course, I was thrilled.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我当然欣喜若狂。

sentence_pairs.en: I wanted to go home.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我想回家。

sentence_pairs.en: But I knew that I had to have a very difficult conversation with Sir Alex.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但我知道，我必须跟弗格森爵士谈一次非常艰难的话。

sentence_pairs.en: There was no buyout clause in my contract, and United could set whatever price they wanted, so I had to convince him to let me go.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我的合同里没有买断条款，曼联想开什么价就开什么价，所以我必须说服他放我走。

sentence_pairs.en: It was one of the hardest conversations of my life, because he took such great care of me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那是我人生中最艰难的对话之一，因为他此前待我那么好。

sentence_pairs.en: But I walked into his office, and I was honest with him.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但我走进他的办公室，对他坦白了。

sentence_pairs.en: I said, “Listen, I feel like I’ve lost your trust.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我说：“听着，我感觉我已经失去了您的信任。

sentence_pairs.en: Barcelona is my home.
sentence_pairs.cn: 巴萨是我的家。

sentence_pairs.en: I want to go back.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我想回去。

sentence_pairs.en: I hope you will let me go.”
sentence_pairs.cn: 我希望您放我走。”

sentence_pairs.en: We had a long conversation, and he decided that I was sincere, and he agreed to let me leave at the end of the season.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我们谈了很久，他认定我是真诚的，同意赛季末放我离开。

sentence_pairs.en: But that’s not the end of our story.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但我们的故事还没完。

sentence_pairs.en: Football can be very complicated.
sentence_pairs.cn: 足球可以是件非常复杂的事。

sentence_pairs.en: At the end of that season, guess who we had to face in the semi finals of the Champions League?
sentence_pairs.cn: 那个赛季末，猜猜我们在欧冠半决赛碰上的是谁？

sentence_pairs.en: Of course, it was Barcelona.
sentence_pairs.cn: 当然是巴萨。

sentence_pairs.en: I had no real chance of playing.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我根本没有上场的机会。

sentence_pairs.en: I was the third-choice centre back.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我是第三号中卫。

sentence_pairs.en: But right before the first leg at the Camp Nou, Nemanja Vidić came down with an injury.
sentence_pairs.cn: 可就在诺坎普首回合开打之前，内马尼亚·维迪奇伤了。

sentence_pairs.en: All of a sudden, I was going to have to step up and play in front of 90,000 people, against my boyhood club.
sentence_pairs.cn: 突然之间，我得站出来，在九万人面前，对阵我少年时代的俱乐部。

sentence_pairs.en: I was excited, nervous, shocked…
sentence_pairs.cn: 我又兴奋，又紧张，又震惊……

sentence_pairs.en: everything.
sentence_pairs.cn: 什么情绪都有。

sentence_pairs.en: Before the match, we had our usual two-hour siesta at the hotel.
sentence_pairs.cn: 赛前我们在酒店照例午休两个小时。

sentence_pairs.en: Of course, I couldn’t sleep.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我当然睡不着。

sentence_pairs.en: All of a sudden, there’s a knock at the door, and I look out the little hole…
sentence_pairs.cn: 突然有人敲门，我从门上的小孔往外看……

sentence_pairs.en: It’s not the maid.
sentence_pairs.cn: 不是客房服务员。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s Sir Alex.
sentence_pairs.cn: 是弗格森爵士。

sentence_pairs.en: I knew something was going on, because he never came to see players before the match.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我知道出事了，因为他从不在赛前找球员。

sentence_pairs.en: I opened the door and he said, “Gerard, I regret to inform you that I can’t play you today.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我打开门，他说：“杰拉德，我很遗憾地通知你，今天我不能派你上场。

sentence_pairs.en: The deal is almost done.
sentence_pairs.cn: 转会快谈成了。

sentence_pairs.en: If I play you, and you have a bad game, they’ll say it’s because you’re headed to Barcelona.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果我让你上场，你又踢砸了，人们会说你是因为要去巴萨。

sentence_pairs.en: So I can’t put you in.
sentence_pairs.cn: 所以我不能用你。

sentence_pairs.en: I just want you to know why.”
sentence_pairs.cn: 我只是想让你知道原因。”

sentence_pairs.en: The truth is, I was pretty devastated.
sentence_pairs.cn: 说实话，我相当崩溃。

sentence_pairs.en: Even though I wanted to go home, I was ready to give everything for United and Sir Alex in that match.
sentence_pairs.cn: 虽然我想回家，但那场比赛我本已准备好为曼联、为弗格森爵士拼上一切。

sentence_pairs.en: It was my dream to play at the Camp Nou in the Champions League.
sentence_pairs.cn: 在诺坎普踢欧冠是我的梦想。

sentence_pairs.en: It hurt very badly.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那一下真的很痛。

sentence_pairs.en: But in the end, Sir Alex made the right decision.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但到头来，弗格森爵士做了正确的决定。

sentence_pairs.en: Everything worked out for the best for everyone.
sentence_pairs.cn: 结果对每个人都好。

sentence_pairs.en: We got a 0-0 draw at the Camp Nou, and then we eliminated Barca at Old Trafford.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我们在诺坎普0比0逼平，然后在老特拉福德淘汰了巴萨。

sentence_pairs.en: We went on to win both the Champions League and the Premier League, and I was able to go home under very good circumstances.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我们接着把欧冠和英超都收入囊中，而我也能在非常体面的处境下回家。

sentence_pairs.en: Because of Sir Alex, I experienced one of the rarest things in football.
sentence_pairs.cn: 因为弗格森爵士，我经历了足球世界里最罕见的事情之一。

sentence_pairs.en: I left in the best way possible.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我以最好的方式离开。

sentence_pairs.en: It didn’t feel like it at the time, but that mistake against Bolton was the best thing to happen in my life.
sentence_pairs.cn: 当时不觉得，但对博尔顿的那次失误，是我人生中发生的最好的事。

sentence_pairs.en: In the end, Barcelona paid only $5 million for me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 最后，巴萨只花了500万美元就把我签了回来。

sentence_pairs.en: I arrived as the fourth-choice center back.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我回来时是第四号中卫。

sentence_pairs.en: No one expected much from me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 没人对我抱什么期望。

sentence_pairs.en: But thanks to Pep Guardiola’s football brain and his belief in me, I was playing alongside Carles Puyol by the end of the season.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但多亏瓜迪奥拉的足球头脑和他对我的信任，赛季末我已经在和卡莱斯·普约尔搭档了。

sentence_pairs.en: Carles took me under his wing and was a huge influence on me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 卡莱斯把我护在翅膀底下，对我影响巨大。

sentence_pairs.en: I learned so much from him, and we formed a partnership that extended to the Spanish national team.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我从他身上学到太多，我们的搭档关系一直延续到西班牙国家队。

sentence_pairs.en: If you would have told me when I returned to Barcelona that, in two years, I would be standing next to Puyol lifting the World Cup trophy, I would have thought you were absolutely crazy.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果我回巴萨的时候你告诉我：两年后，我会站在普约尔身边举起世界杯——我一定觉得你彻底疯了。

sentence_pairs.en: But football is a funny business, and that is exactly what happened.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但足球就是这么有意思的行当，事情恰恰就这样发生了。

sentence_pairs.en: That’s how quickly everything changed for me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我的境遇变化就是这么快。

sentence_pairs.en: And it really makes me think about fate.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这真的让我思考命运。

sentence_pairs.en: If I don’t make that mistake against Bolton, does it work out that way?
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果我没有在对博尔顿的比赛里犯那个错，事情还会这样发展吗？

sentence_pairs.en: If Sir Alex decides to keep me on for another season to get a bigger transfer fee for me, does it work out that way?
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果弗格森爵士为了多卖我一笔转会费而把我多留一个赛季，事情还会这样发展吗？

sentence_pairs.en: There are so many things that happen in a footballer’s life that people don’t see.
sentence_pairs.cn: 球员的人生里有太多人们看不见的事。

sentence_pairs.en: And that’s why I’m writing this.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这正是我写下这些的原因。

sentence_pairs.en: And that is why I need to tell you another quick story…
sentence_pairs.cn: 这也是为什么我还需要再给你讲一个小故事……

sentence_pairs.en: Because, as I said, football is very complicated.
sentence_pairs.cn: 因为正如我说的，足球非常复杂。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s not like the movies.
sentence_pairs.cn: 它不像电影。

sentence_pairs.en: When I was 24 years old, I was on top of the world.
sentence_pairs.cn: 二十四岁那年，我站在世界之巅。

sentence_pairs.en: I had won everything — La Liga, Champions League, World Cup.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我什么都赢过了——西甲、欧冠、世界杯。

sentence_pairs.en: I was playing under a genius manager in Pep Guardiola, who really believed in me from the moment I arrived.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我在一个天才主教练瓜迪奥拉手下踢球，他从我到来的那一刻就真的信任我。

sentence_pairs.en: I was playing for the club I had loved since I was a boy.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我效力的是我从小爱着的俱乐部。

sentence_pairs.en: It was perfect.
sentence_pairs.cn: 一切完美。

sentence_pairs.en: And then…
sentence_pairs.cn: 然后……

sentence_pairs.en: I had the worst season of my career.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我迎来了职业生涯最糟糕的一个赛季。

sentence_pairs.en: Everything seemed to fall apart in 2012.
sentence_pairs.cn: 2012年，一切仿佛崩塌了。

sentence_pairs.en: I don’t know why.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我不知道为什么。

sentence_pairs.en: Perhaps I had lost the fear that drove me to that level.
sentence_pairs.cn: 也许我丢失了那股把我推到那个高度的恐惧感。

sentence_pairs.en: But for whatever reason, I started questioning myself.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但不管什么原因，我开始怀疑自己。

sentence_pairs.en: As the season went on, Pep started to lose faith in me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 随着赛季推进，瓜迪奥拉开始对我失去信心。

sentence_pairs.en: For the first three seasons, we had a phenomenal relationship.
sentence_pairs.cn: 头三个赛季，我们的关系好得不得了。

sentence_pairs.en: I still revere Pep as a manager.
sentence_pairs.cn: 至今我仍敬重瓜帅这个教练。

sentence_pairs.en: But the truth is, it was an extremely hard time.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但说实话，那是一段极其艰难的时期。

sentence_pairs.en: He wanted his players to be obsessed with football 24 hours a day, and at that point in my life, I didn’t understand it.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他要球员一天24小时都为足球痴迷，而在人生的那个阶段，我不理解这一点。

sentence_pairs.en: I wasn’t as committed to that philosophy.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我没有那么认同那套哲学。

sentence_pairs.en: Pep simply didn’t trust me anymore, and the crucial moment was when he decided not to play me against Real Madrid in the league.
sentence_pairs.cn: 瓜帅就是不再信任我了，关键时刻是他决定在联赛里对皇马不让我上场。

sentence_pairs.en: That was crushing to me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那对我打击巨大。

sentence_pairs.en: I started to think, Is this it?
sentence_pairs.cn: 我开始想：就这样了吗？

sentence_pairs.en: Is the dream of playing for Barca over?
sentence_pairs.cn: 为巴萨踢球的梦就这么结束了？

sentence_pairs.en: Is this how fast it can go away?
sentence_pairs.cn: 一切消逝得能这么快？

sentence_pairs.en: Then, in the second leg of the Champions League semifinal against Chelsea, something pretty crazy happened.
sentence_pairs.cn: 然后，欧冠半决赛对切尔西的第二回合，一件相当疯狂的事发生了。

sentence_pairs.en: Another turn of fate.
sentence_pairs.cn: 又一次命运的转弯。

sentence_pairs.en: We had lost 1–0 in the first leg at Stamford Bridge, and I didn’t play.
sentence_pairs.cn: 首回合我们在斯坦福桥0比1输了，我没有上场。

sentence_pairs.en: Pep started me in the second leg at the Camp Nou to try to turn things around, but I honestly cannot tell you anything about the match.
sentence_pairs.cn: 第二回合在诺坎普，瓜帅让我首发，想力挽狂澜——但说实话，那场比赛的任何事我都讲不出来。

sentence_pairs.en: Early on in the game, our keeper, Víctor Valdés, accidentally kneed me in the head during a clearance.
sentence_pairs.cn: 比赛early阶段，我们的门将维克托·巴尔德斯解围时一膝盖撞在我头上。

sentence_pairs.en: I was knocked completely unconscious.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我彻底失去了意识。

sentence_pairs.en: When I got to my feet, I stayed in the game somehow, and I know that I ran around for about 10 minutes, but I truly cannot remember anything that happened.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我爬起来，不知怎么继续留在场上，我知道自己又跑了大概十分钟，但我真的完全不记得发生了什么。

sentence_pairs.en: Eventually, the doctor noticed that I was struggling and they pulled me out and put me on a stretcher and rushed me to the hospital.
sentence_pairs.cn: 最后队医看出我不对劲，把我抬上担架，火速送去了医院。

sentence_pairs.en: I woke up the next day, and I couldn’t remember anything from the match.
sentence_pairs.cn: 第二天醒来，比赛的事我一点都想不起来。

sentence_pairs.en: I couldn’t even remember who won.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我连谁赢了都不记得。

sentence_pairs.en: I was in a complete fog.
sentence_pairs.cn: 整个人一片迷雾。

sentence_pairs.en: It turns out, the match ended 2–2, and we were knocked out.
sentence_pairs.cn: 后来才知道，那场球2比2，我们被淘汰了。

sentence_pairs.en: Within a few days, Pep announced his departure from Barca.
sentence_pairs.cn: 几天之内，瓜帅宣布离开巴萨。

sentence_pairs.en: It felt like an era was coming to an end, and I thought that perhaps my time was up, too.
sentence_pairs.cn: 感觉一个时代要落幕了，我寻思也许我的时代也到头了。

sentence_pairs.en: That season really made me think about my career, and my life.
sentence_pairs.cn: 那个赛季真的让我重新审视我的职业生涯，和我的人生。

sentence_pairs.en: It was a wake-up call.
sentence_pairs.cn: 它是一记警钟。

sentence_pairs.en: When our team was playing for it all, Pep didn’t believe in me anymore.
sentence_pairs.cn: 当球队为一切而战的时候，瓜帅不再相信我。

sentence_pairs.en: Then, when he finally turned to me, I got knocked out cold.
sentence_pairs.cn: 等他终于肯用我的时候，我被打得不省人事。

sentence_pairs.en: Sometimes I think about what would have happened if I had woken up the next day and found out that we had gone through against Chelsea.
sentence_pairs.cn: 有时我会想，如果第二天醒来，我得知我们淘汰了切尔西晋级了，会怎么样。

sentence_pairs.en: I was out with a head injury for weeks, so I definitely wouldn’t have played in the final.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我因为头部伤势缺席了几周，决赛我肯定打不了。

sentence_pairs.en: Maybe we would have won the Champions League.
sentence_pairs.cn: 也许我们会赢下那届欧冠。

sentence_pairs.en: Maybe Pep would have decided to stay at Barca.
sentence_pairs.cn: 也许瓜帅会决定留在巴萨。

sentence_pairs.en: Maybe he never would have regained his trust in me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 也许他永远不会重新信任我。

sentence_pairs.en: Maybe I would be at another club right now.
sentence_pairs.cn: 也许我现在人在另一家俱乐部。

sentence_pairs.en: Instead, Tito Vilanova arrived as the manager the next season, and he gave me a chance to regain my place.
sentence_pairs.cn: 现实是，下一个赛季蒂托·比拉诺瓦来了，他给了我夺回位置的机会。

sentence_pairs.en: There are so many moments like this that happen during a long career that make you think about fate, and chance, and how things could have gone differently.
sentence_pairs.cn: 漫长的职业生涯里，有太多这样的时刻，让你思考命运、机缘，以及事情本可能怎样不同。

sentence_pairs.en: But that’s not what we read in the headlines.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但这不是头条里的世界。

sentence_pairs.en: In the headlines, things are simple.
sentence_pairs.cn: 在头条里，事情都很简单。

sentence_pairs.en: In real life, the most interesting things are happening beneath the surface.
sentence_pairs.cn: 在真实生活里，最有意思的东西都藏在表面之下。

sentence_pairs.en: For example, people often ask me what it has been like playing with Messi for so many years.
sentence_pairs.cn: 举个例子，人们总问我，和梅西一起踢了这么多年球是什么感受。

sentence_pairs.en: If I had to explain it in one sentence: He is an alien.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果要我用一句话解释：他是外星人。

sentence_pairs.en: He is not from this planet.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他不是这个星球的人。

sentence_pairs.en: He’s the only player that I can recall seeing play for the first time, way back when we were 13 years old, and saying to myself, “Oh, this kid comes from somewhere else.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他是我唯一记得的、第一次看就让我对自己说“哦，这孩子是从别处来的”的球员——那时我们才十三岁。

sentence_pairs.en: This is not human.”
sentence_pairs.cn: 这不是人类。

sentence_pairs.en: He is an assassin.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他是个刺客。

sentence_pairs.en: He’s the greatest I’ve ever seen.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他是我见过最伟大的球员。

sentence_pairs.en: But, you see, it’s not about the way he attacks.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但你看，关键不在他的进攻。

sentence_pairs.en: People ask me, “What’s the most incredible thing I’ve seen Leo do on the pitch?” And they expect me to tell them about him dribbling three defenders.
sentence_pairs.cn: 人们问我：“你在场上见过莱奥做的最不可思议的事是什么？”他们期待我讲他连过三名后卫的故事。

sentence_pairs.en: And trust me, I have plenty of those stories.
sentence_pairs.cn: 放心，那种故事我有一箩筐。

sentence_pairs.en: But for me, the reason that I know he’s from another planet is because of what happens when he doesn’t have the ball.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但对我来说，我知道他来自另一个星球的证据，是他无球时发生的事。

sentence_pairs.en: Perhaps you can’t see it on TV, but I can see it on the pitch.
sentence_pairs.cn: 在电视上你也许看不见，但在球场上我看得见。

sentence_pairs.en: You have to see his face when he’s sprinting to win the ball back from a defender.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你必须看他的脸——当他冲刺着从后卫脚下把球抢回来的时候。

sentence_pairs.en: He has a look in his eyes that I haven’t ever seen in another footballer.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他眼里的那种神情，我在任何别的球员身上都没见过。

sentence_pairs.en: It is what makes him so great.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这正是他伟大的原因。

sentence_pairs.en: He is not interested in the spectacle.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他对表演没有兴趣。

sentence_pairs.en: He rarely even does stepovers.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他甚至很少踩单车。

sentence_pairs.en: He’s cut from a different cloth.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他根本就不是同一种材料造出来的。

sentence_pairs.en: His greatness is in his obsession with winning the ball.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他的伟大，藏在他对抢回皮球的痴迷里。

sentence_pairs.en: Maybe that doesn’t make for a great headline.
sentence_pairs.cn: 也许这上不了大标题。

sentence_pairs.en: But when I think about Messi’s true magic, it’s not in something you can find on YouTube.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但当我想到梅西真正的魔力，它不是你在 YouTube 上能搜到的东西。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s about a subtle expression in his eyes.
sentence_pairs.cn: 它在他眼里一闪而过的细微神情。

sentence_pairs.en: His greatness would take me another 5,000 words to explain.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他的伟大够我再写五千字。

sentence_pairs.en: Perhaps in another article!
sentence_pairs.cn: 也许下篇文章再写吧！

sentence_pairs.en: And that brings me back to the beginning.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这又把话题带回了开头。

sentence_pairs.en: As I get older and prepare for the final World Cup of my career, I have been thinking about my place in the world.
sentence_pairs.cn: 年纪渐长，着手准备职业生涯最后一届世界杯，我一直在思考自己在这个世界上的位置。

sentence_pairs.en: I have been thinking about how I got here, and what else I want to accomplish in life.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我一直在想我是怎么走到今天的，以及这辈子我还想完成什么。

sentence_pairs.en: As athletes, I believe that we should use our platform to connect with people and let them into our lives and into our minds a little bit more.
sentence_pairs.cn: 作为运动员，我认为我们应该善用自己的平台，和人们连接，让他们更多走进我们的生活、我们的头脑。

sentence_pairs.en: I think this mentality is needed now more than ever.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我觉得这种心态现在比以往任何时候都更需要。

sentence_pairs.en: If you watch television in Madrid, the media will tell you that everyone in Barcelona is trying to destroy the country.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果你在马德里看电视，媒体会告诉你，巴塞罗那的所有人都在试图毁掉这个国家。

sentence_pairs.en: If you watch television in Barcelona, they will tell you that everyone in Madrid is trying to oppress the people.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果你在巴塞罗那看电视，他们会告诉你，马德里的所有人都在试图压迫人民。

sentence_pairs.en: Everyone is the bad guy now, depending on where you watch TV.
sentence_pairs.cn: 现在，坏人在哪边都有，就看你电视开在哪个台。

sentence_pairs.en: They say the national team is in turmoil because of political differences.
sentence_pairs.cn: 他们说国家队因为政治分歧陷入动荡。

sentence_pairs.en: In truth, we almost never talk about politics.
sentence_pairs.cn: 实际上，我们几乎从不聊政治。

sentence_pairs.en: I’m too busy telling the Real guys that they’re f***ed in the league, and they’re too busy talking to me about refereeing conspiracies!
sentence_pairs.cn: 我忙着告诉皇马那帮人这赛季你们完蛋了，他们也忙着跟我掰扯裁判阴谋论呢！

sentence_pairs.en: I’ve been a footballer for more than half my life.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我当球员的时间，已经超过人生的一半。

sentence_pairs.en: I’m 31 years old now.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我今年31岁。

sentence_pairs.en: I used to say that I would be retired by 30.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我从前总说自己三十岁就退役。

sentence_pairs.en: Honestly, do you know what keeps me going?
sentence_pairs.cn: 说实话，你知道是什么让我继续踢下去吗？

sentence_pairs.en: It’s the experiences I’ve had in the locker rooms.
sentence_pairs.cn: 是我在更衣室里经历的那些事。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s getting to know footballing geniuses like Messi, and Puyol, and Neymar, and Roy Keane (even though he almost murdered me).
sentence_pairs.cn: 是能够认识梅西、普约尔、内马尔这样的足球天才，还有罗伊·基恩（尽管他差点杀了我）。

sentence_pairs.en: In the end, football is a long trip.
sentence_pairs.cn: 说到底，足球是一场漫长的旅行。

sentence_pairs.en: You win.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你会赢。

sentence_pairs.en: You lose.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你会输。

sentence_pairs.en: You embarrass yourself.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你会出丑。

sentence_pairs.en: You make mistakes.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你会犯错。

sentence_pairs.en: You laugh, you cry.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你笑，你哭。

sentence_pairs.en: You do dumb things to pass the time.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你干各种傻事打发时间。

sentence_pairs.en: Maybe you and your teammates even set an assistant coach’s motorcycle on fire (before buying him a brand new one, of course…
sentence_pairs.cn: 说不定你们全队还会把助理教练的摩托车点着了火（当然，事后又给他买了辆全新的……

sentence_pairs.en: I’ll leave that story for another time!)
sentence_pairs.cn: 这个故事改天再讲！）

sentence_pairs.en: Hopefully, you grow from a boy to a man.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但愿你从一个男孩长成了一个男人。

sentence_pairs.en: This is what makes sports beautiful, for me.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这就是体育之于我的美。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s all just one long story.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这一切，本就是一个漫长的故事。

sentence_pairs.en: Welcome to The Players’ Tribune Global.
sentence_pairs.cn: 欢迎来到《球员论坛报》全球版。

sentence_pairs.en: One of my goals is to never shut up.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我的目标之一，是永远不闭嘴。

sentences.en: I’m going to let you in on a little inside information.
sentences.cn: 我要跟你们说一点内部消息。

sentences.en: Everybody knows that footballers have text groups on WhatsApp.
sentences.cn: 大家都知道，球员们 WhatsApp 上都有各种小群。

sentences.en: I have one just for my friends from home, and I have another just for my Barca teammates.
sentences.cn: 我有一个只有老家朋友们的群，还有一个只有巴萨队友的群。

sentences.en: But my favorite one might surprise you.
sentences.cn: 但我最喜欢的一个群，可能会让你们吃惊。

sentences.en: Earlier this season, when we were already 8 or 9 points clear of Real Madrid in the league, I started a special group for some of the guys on the Spanish national team who play for Real Madrid and Barcelona.
sentences.cn: 本赛季早些时候，当我们已经在联赛里领先皇马八九分的时候，我建了一个特别的群，把西班牙国家队里效力皇马和巴萨的几个家伙都拉了进去。

sentences.en: If you only read what the media says, you would think that we hate one another.
sentences.cn: 如果你只看媒体怎么写，你会以为我们互相恨透了对方。

sentences.en: But, in fact, we all get along really well, and we text back and forth about tactics and football philosophies and even the books we’re reading.
sentences.cn: 但事实上，我们处得非常好，会在群里聊战术、聊足球哲学，甚至连最近在读什么书都聊。

sentences.en: No, come on, of course I’m joking!
sentences.cn: 不，得了吧，我当然是开玩笑的！

sentences.en: All we do in that group is talk shit to one another about Barça and Real!
sentences.cn: 那个群里我们干的事，就是互相损巴萨和皇马！

sentences.en: It’s the best.
sentences.cn: 太好玩了。

sentences.en: We’re just like little kids.
sentences.cn: 我们就像一群小孩子。

sentences.en: And the truth is, it’s especially hilarious for me right now, because now we’re up 15 points on Real in the league.
sentences.cn: 而且说实话，现在这个节点对我来说尤其好笑，因为我们在联赛里已经领先皇马15分了。

sentences.en: So I’m getting very creative in my responses.
sentences.cn: 所以我回消息的创意，是越来越足了。

sentences.en: Last season, when the Real guys were winning everything, they were feeling pretty good.
sentences.cn: 上赛季皇马那帮人赢麻了的时候，他们感觉相当良好。

sentences.en: They were talking shit constantly whenever I saw them at national team training.
sentences.cn: 国家队集训一见面，他们就逮着机会不停地损我。

sentences.en: Man, every time they won a match last season, they were posting shirtless photos on Instagram from the locker room.
sentences.cn: 兄弟，上赛季他们每赢一场球，就在 Instagram 上发更衣室里的裸上身合照。

sentences.en: Remember that?
sentences.cn: 还记得吗？

sentences.en: They were smiling and flexing their muscles like The Rock and saying #HalaMadrid and posting little trophy emojis.
sentences.cn: 他们笑着秀肌肉，跟巨石强森似的，配文 #HalaMadrid，再发几个小奖杯的表情。

sentences.en: This season, though, it’s a different vibe.
sentences.cn: 不过这个赛季，画风变了。

sentences.en: All their Instagram photos are looking very somber.
sentences.cn: 他们的 Instagram 照片看上去非常沉重。

sentences.en: “3 points today.
sentences.cn: “今天拿下3分。

sentences.en: We must keep working harder!”
sentences.cn: 我们必须更加努力！”

sentences.en: So I’m texting them in the WhatsApp group, “Come on guys, why so serious?!”
sentences.cn: 于是我在 WhatsApp 群里问他们：“各位各位，干嘛这么严肃呀？！”

sentences.en: Then I put a little crying emoji, and a laughing emoji.
sentences.cn: 然后我再补一个小声哭泣的表情，和一个笑哭的表情。

sentences.en: I even made a special name for the group.
sentences.cn: 我甚至给那个群起了个专用名。

sentences.en: It’s called: CONGRATULATIONS.
sentences.cn: 叫：CONGRATULATIONS（恭喜恭喜）。

sentences.en: I can joke around with those guys, because they are my brothers on the Spanish national team.
sentences.cn: 我能跟那帮家伙开玩笑，因为他们在西班牙国家队是我的兄弟。

sentences.en: We might hate each other’s clubs, but we are all playing for the same country, with the same dream, and that’s something that I’m very, very proud of.
sentences.cn: 我们或许恨死了对方的俱乐部，但我们为同一个国家而战，怀着同一个梦想，这一点让我非常、非常自豪。

sentences.en: Ever since I was a little boy watching Luis Enrique bleed all over his jersey at the’94 World Cup, my dream was to play for the national team.
sentences.cn: 从小看着路易斯·恩里克在94年世界杯上球衣浸满鲜血的样子，我的梦想就是为国家队效力。

sentences.en: I’m extremely proud to wear the badge every four years at the World Cup.
sentences.cn: 每四年能披上国家队战袍征战世界杯，我自豪至极。

sentences.en: Maybe that will surprise some people.
sentences.cn: 这可能会让一些人吃惊。

sentences.en: If you watch television in Madrid, they’ll tell you a very different story about me.
sentences.cn: 如果你在马德里看电视，他们会讲一个关于我的完全不同的故事。

sentences.en: They’ll say that I’m a traitor, and that I want to tear the country apart because of my public support for the Catalan people’s right to vote in the independence referendum.
sentences.cn: 他们会说我是叛徒，说我因为公开支持加泰罗尼亚人民投票独立的权利，就想撕裂这个国家。

sentences.en: I have never even commented on how I would vote.
sentences.cn: 可我连自己会投哪一票都从没公开评论过。

sentences.en: I am not trying to be a politician and sway people.
sentences.cn: 我不是要当政治家，也不是要左右别人。

sentences.en: What I believe is irrelevant.
sentences.cn: 我信什么并不重要。

sentences.en: I am just one opinion out of millions.
sentences.cn: 我只是几百万种意见中的一种。

sentences.en: But what I do believe is that the 7.5 million people from my homeland of Catalonia have the right to vote on this question in a peaceful manner.
sentences.cn: 但我确实相信，我家乡加泰罗尼亚的750万人，有权利以和平的方式就这个问题投票。

sentences.en: The issue is very complicated, and it requires a lot of thought and debate.
sentences.cn: 这个问题非常复杂，需要大量的思考与辩论。

sentences.en: It’s a tricky position for me to be in, personally, because the happiest moment of my life was winning the World Cup for Spain, but on the other hand, being Catalan is in my blood.
sentences.cn: 就我个人而言，这是个为难处境：因为我人生中最幸福的时刻，是为西班牙赢得世界杯；可另一方面，加泰罗尼亚人在我的血液里。

sentences.en: That’s my people, my heritage, my land.
sentences.cn: 那是我的同胞，我的传承，我的土地。

sentences.en: And when 80% of people in Catalonia say they want the right to vote, I believe they should be heard.
sentences.cn: 当加泰罗尼亚80%的人说他们想要投票的权利，我认为他们应该被倾听。

sentences.en: If that opinion makes my own countrymen dislike me…
sentences.cn: 如果这个立场让我自己的同胞讨厌我……

sentences.en: well, I am perfectly tranquil with that thought.
sentences.cn: 好吧，这个念头我也完全安然。

sentences.en: It’s funny, I noticed some people in America have started telling the NBA players to “just shut up and dribble” when they express their opinions on real problems in society.
sentences.cn: 有意思的是，我注意到美国已经有人开始对NBA球员说“你只管闭嘴运你的球”，不让他们对社会上的真实问题发表看法。

sentences.en: It’s ridiculous, no?
sentences.cn: 很荒谬，不是吗？

sentences.en: It’s the same here in Spain.
sentences.cn: 西班牙这里也一个样。

sentences.en: They say, “Just shut up and play football.
sentences.cn: 他们说：“你只管闭嘴踢球。

sentences.en: It’s all you know.”
sentences.cn: 你懂的只有足球。”

sentences.en: Sorry, but I will not just shut up and play.
sentences.cn: 抱歉，我不会闭嘴，也不会只顾踢球。

sentences.en: It’s not all I know.
sentences.cn: 足球不是我懂的全部。

sentences.en: There’s a lot more depth to footballers than most people realize, and I think it’s important that we express ourselves and our views.
sentences.cn: 球员的内心远比大多数人以为的丰富，我认为我们表达自己和自己的观点很重要。

sentences.en: Footballers are human beings, and that is something that is being lost in the media world that we live in today.
sentences.cn: 球员也是人——在今天的媒体世界里，这一点正在被遗忘。

sentences.en: There are things going on in our lives that the public has no idea about.
sentences.cn: 我们的生活里发生着许多公众完全不知道的事。

sentences.en: Yes, you can google match results, and you can google transfer rumors, but you can’t google how a person feels, or what motivates them, or what they fear.
sentences.cn: 是的，你可以谷歌比赛结果，可以谷歌转会传闻，但你谷歌不到一个人的感受、他的动力，或者他的恐惧。

sentences.en: Let me give you some examples from my own life.
sentences.cn: 让我拿自己人生里的一些例子来说吧。

sentences.en: I look back on the last 10 years of my career, and I’ve won the World Cup, the Champions League, La Liga, the Spanish Cup…
sentences.cn: 回望我职业生涯的这十年，我拿过世界杯、欧冠、西甲、国王杯……

sentences.en: I’ve won it all, as I like to remind my Madrid friends on WhatsApp?
sentences.cn: 该拿的我都拿遍了——这一点我很乐意在 WhatsApp 上提醒我的皇马朋友们？

sentences.en: But 10 years ago, I was almost f***ed.
sentences.cn: 但十年前，我差点就完蛋了。

sentences.en: My whole life could have turned out very different if it wasn’t for Sir Alex Ferguson.
sentences.cn: 如果不是亚历克斯·弗格森爵士，我整个人生可能是完全另一个样子。

sentences.en: I arrived at Manchester United a boy, and I left a man.
sentences.cn: 我以一个男孩的身份来到曼联，离开时已经是个男人。

sentences.en: It was a crazy time for me, because I had never been away from home before.
sentences.cn: 那段时间对我来说是疯狂的，因为我之前从来没有离开过家。

sentences.en: I spent my first 17 years growing up in Spain in Barcelona’s youth academy, and it almost felt like I was playing for the local school team or something.
sentences.cn: 我人生的前十七年在西班牙巴塞罗那的青训学院里长大，在那里踢球几乎就像在校队踢着玩。

sentences.en: I knew everybody there, and I was close to my family.
sentences.cn: 那里的人我全都认识，家人也近在身边。

sentences.en: So, to me, football was just fun.
sentences.cn: 所以对我来说，足球就是纯粹的乐趣。

sentences.en: I didn’t understand the business side of the game at all.
sentences.cn: 这门生意的另一面，我完全不懂。

sentences.en: Then I arrived at United, and honestly, it was a complete shock.
sentences.cn: 然后我到了曼联，说实话，受到了彻底的冲击。

sentences.en: One of my very first matches at Old Trafford, we were in the dressing room getting ready, and I was nervous as hell.
sentences.cn: 我在老特拉福德的头几场比赛之一，我们在更衣室里做准备，我紧张得要死。

sentences.en: Imagine it — I’m 18 years old, and I’m sitting in that little dressing room putting on my socks next to Ruud Van Nistelrooy and Ryan Giggs and Rio Ferdinand.
sentences.cn: 想象一下——我十八岁，坐在那间小更衣室里穿球袜，旁边是范尼斯特鲁伊、瑞恩·吉格斯和里奥·费迪南德。

sentences.en: I wanted to be invisible.
sentences.cn: 我恨不得自己隐身。

sentences.en: I was thinking, Just do your job and go unnoticed.
sentences.cn: 我心想：做好你的事，别被人注意到。

sentences.en: So we’re sitting there waiting for the gaffer to come in and speak to us, and I’m literally sitting right next to Roy Keane.
sentences.cn: 我们坐在那儿等主教练进来训话，而我就坐在罗伊·基恩的正旁边。

sentences.en: The dressing room is so small that our legs are almost touching.
sentences.cn: 那间更衣室小到我们的腿几乎要碰到一起。

sentences.en: There’s no space at all.
sentences.cn: 一点空隙都没有。

sentences.en: It’s dead quiet.
sentences.cn: 鸦雀无声。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, you could hear this little vibration.
sentences.cn: 突然，你听见一阵轻微的震动声。

sentences.en: Very soft.
sentences.cn: 很轻很轻。

sentences.en: Bzzzzzz……
sentences.cn: 嗡嗡嗡……

sentences.en: Bzzzzzzz.
sentences.cn: 嗡嗡嗡。

sentences.en: Roy is looking around the room.
sentences.cn: 罗伊环视整间屋子。

sentences.en: Bzzzzzzz…..
sentences.cn: 嗡嗡嗡嗡……

sentences.en: Oh, shit.
sentences.cn: 坏了。

sentences.en: I realize it’s me.
sentences.cn: 我发现是我。

sentences.en: It’s my cell phone.
sentences.cn: 是我的手机。

sentences.en: I left it on vibrate, and it’s in the pocket of my pants, stuffed in the clothes bag that’s hanging right behind Roy’s head.
sentences.cn: 我忘了关，调的震动，手机在裤子口袋里，裤子塞在衣物袋里，而那个袋子就挂在罗伊脑袋后面。

sentences.en: Roy can’t find where the noise is coming from.
sentences.cn: 罗伊找不到声音是从哪来的。

sentences.en: Now he’s looking around the room like a maniac.
sentences.cn: 这下他像个疯子一样满屋子看。

sentences.en: His eyes are darting everywhere, and he’s trying to figure it out.
sentences.cn: 他的眼珠子四处乱转，拼命想搞明白。

sentences.en: You know the famous scene with Jack Nicholson in The Shining, when he bursts through the door?
sentences.cn: 你知道《闪灵》里杰克·尼科尔森破门而入的那个著名镜头吗？

sentences.en: That’s what he looked like.
sentences.cn: 他当时就是那副样子。

sentences.en: He screams out to everybody, “Whose phone is that?!”
sentences.cn: 他对着所有人吼：“那是谁的手机？！”

sentences.en: Silence.
sentences.cn: 一片寂静。

sentences.en: He asks again.
sentences.cn: 他又问了一遍。

sentences.en: Silence.
sentences.cn: 寂静。

sentences.en: He asks a third time.
sentences.cn: 他问了第三遍。

sentences.en: “Whose.
Bloody.
sentences.cn: 到底。
是TM的。

sentences.en: Phone.
sentences.cn: 谁的。

sentences.en: Is.
sentences.cn: 手机。

sentences.en: That?!”
Finally, I spoke up, like a little boy.
sentences.cn: 最后，我像个小学生一样开了口。

sentences.en: Very softly, I said, “I’m so sorry.
sentences.cn: 声音小得很，我说：“对不起。

sentences.en: It’s mine.”
sentences.cn: 是我的。”

sentences.en: Roy put his arm around me, and he laughed, and he told me not to worry about it.
sentences.cn: 罗伊搂住我，笑了起来，叫我别放在心上。

sentences.en: No, come on, of course I’m joking!
sentences.cn: 不，得了吧，我当然是开玩笑的！

sentences.en: Roy lost his mind!
sentences.cn: 罗伊炸了！

sentences.en: He went nuts in front of everybody!
sentences.cn: 他当着所有人的面暴怒！

sentences.en: It was incredible.
sentences.cn: 场面太震撼了。

sentences.en: I almost shit myself.
sentences.cn: 我差点尿裤子。

sentences.en: But it was a good lesson.
sentences.cn: 但那是很好的一课。

sentences.en: Now, in 2018, everything is different.
sentences.cn: 现在，2018年，一切都不同了。

sentences.en: All these kids are on their iPhones before the matches.
sentences.cn: 比赛前孩子们都捧着 iPhone。

sentences.en: But back then, in 2006?
